title: Book One · Chapter 112: One and Two Come In
story:
The crates arrive just after lunch.

Mr Han holds one end of the first. Mr Qiu holds the other. Dad comes home for his meal. He helps carry the crate through the gate. Then he must go back to work.

Ronan and Leo stand out of the carrying path. Their job is to keep two paper lists dry. The adults will put the crates down first. Then the boys can hand Mr Qiu the lists. He needs his hands free for the crates now.

“Do not walk backwards under their feet,” Mum says.

Leo moves beside the wall. Ronan stays by the kitchen door. Ronan stands and waits. He wants a job too. Then Mr Han asks for the gate to open wider. Mum can help with the gate.

Mum opens it. The adults turn the first crate carefully. It fits with a small space on each side.

Two folded cloths mark the place in Mrs Lan's room. Dad checked some short wooden supports. The crates stand on these. They stay away from the damp outer wall. The cupboard can still open. The walking line to Mrs Lan's chair remains clear.

Mr Qiu opens crate one. It holds wrapped exercise books and packets of writing paper. Crate two has pencils, rulers and rubbers. There are a few small boxes of clips too.

Ronan reads the list. He stops at the word rubbers for a moment. Leo points, then waits for him to say it himself.

Mr Qiu checks each line against the stock. No money box comes into the children's hands. He keeps his private papers and money with him.

At the bottom of the second list, Ronan sees a blank space. He wants to add the six wet books there.

“They are not in this crate,” Mr Qiu says.

“Where will they go?”

“I will ask Miss Wu for space at school. Perhaps we can lay them flat to dry there. They are new exercise books. No one's private writing is inside.”

Mum will take Ronan to school the next morning. She offers to speak to Miss Wu then. Mr Qiu will send only the damp books, not the whole stall.

He checks both lists and puts them in a folder. It rests on the dry crates. Mrs Lan asks for the crate numbers to keep. She needs his contact address too. They write that on a separate card for her drawer.

Then she wants her room back.

The boys thank her and leave. Leo stops in the yard.

“Can people buy things here now?”

“Not yet,” Mum says. “She agreed to store boxes. That was the agreement.”

Ronan looks at the green gate. It is not wide enough for a crowd of customers. He imagines customers at Mrs Lan's cupboard. Perhaps they want to look inside by mistake. He laughs at the thought of cupboard customers. Then he looks at the narrow gate again. Mrs Lan was right to ask about the space.

In the afternoon, Mr Qiu returns to the closed stall. Mr Han goes with him to check it. The front board stays up. The adults still need to deal with the roof. Mr Qiu still needs to choose a new selling place.

Ronan makes a little drawing for his own folder. He copies the two crate numbers onto it. He does not draw every packet inside. Mr Qiu has the real list.

Before supper, Mrs Lan calls him into her room. He left his pencil on her table. She asks him to move it. He takes it at once. Mrs Lan agreed to keep the two large crates. Ronan did not ask her to keep his pencil. He puts it back in his own tin.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- supports＝垫托物
- store＝存放
- private papers＝私人文件
- contact address＝联络地址

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：rubbers＝橡皮；clips＝回形针；crate＝木箱。

## 读句提示

**Then the boys can hand Mr Qiu the lists.**

然后／男孩们能把清单／递给Mr Qiu。成人先放稳木箱。

## 理解问题

1. 两个木箱分别装着什么？
2. 保管木箱为什么不等于同意在屋内卖东西？
